title: Wayfinding is not signage — Image Wiki

rules.rule: Place information only at decision points (junctions/turns) rather than repeating messages along straight corridors.
rules.evidence: Between decisions, a walker needs nothing; they are already going the right way.

rules.rule: Provide confirmation after a turn to stop anxious doubling-back, and ensure recovery signs exist for wrong turns.
rules.evidence: Having made the turn, the walker needs to know they were right. The standard requires that on reaching the platform a customer can see a sign confirming the platform number and direction.

rules.rule: Express scale in walking minutes rather than metres because people use time to decide whether to walk.
rules.evidence: Legible London expresses scale in walking minutes, because research showed that is what people use when deciding whether to walk.
